member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.AiActivationClaims
member.summary: The level's activation claims — the global list at dword_5BDA28 that keeps two guards from running to the same alarm panel.

remarks.para: AIAction_Activate's start (0x48E620) tests the target task against this list (sub_4532D0) and skips the whole action when it is already claimed; otherwise it adds the task (sub_453300(task, 1)) — and, when the target is the AI's own alarm trigger, the alarm control too — keeping the claim handles at HumanAI+15024/+15028. The action's end function (0x48E870) and the AI's own death cleanup (0x44F410 at 0x44FAD2/0x44FAEB) release them, so a guard shot on the way frees the panel for the next one.
Only the AI module reads the list — membership means "an activation is under way", not "the task has been activated".

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.AiAlarmControlState
member.summary: An AlarmControl's two-tick alarm state, and the rule that turns it into and .

remarks.para: From the update at 0x4408A0. The task keeps two flags — +673 is the alarm's state this tick and +674 is the previous tick's value of +673, shadowed at the top of the update before the new value is computed. It is the same Last-shadow edge-detection pattern M3 found in the script variable registry, and the determinism contract already requires reproducing it.
That corrects a misreading of the two accessors. 0x440C00 and 0x440C10 look like "is on" and "is off"; they are is on and was on. The consequence is the interesting part — the AI's per-tick does
remarks.code: if (IsOn(ctrl)) { post AIEVENT_ALARMON; alert = 1; } else if (WasOn(ctrl)) { post AIEVENT_ALARMOFF; }
remarks.para: so is level-triggered — posted every tick the alarm is on, which is also what keeps the AI's alert latch set — while is a falling edge, posted on exactly the one tick after the alarm stops. An AI that misses that single tick (because a higher-priority event took the dispatch, and undispatched events are discarded) never hears the all-clear.

The state itself comes from two script condition expressions, which are the task type's only two parameters and occupy the tail of its 848-byte instance exactly: one at +684 (80 bytes) sets a flag and stamps the tick into +676, and one at +764 (84 bytes) sets . Two disable gates at +400 and +576 force both to false without evaluating either.

remarks.para: The faction prefix means nothing to the dispatch — MAFIA_GUARD_AK and GUARD_AK both land on the guard arm, exactly as they run byte-identical scripts. What decides is GUARD against PATROL.

This is the correction that matters most to how the game plays. The port gave every soldier the guard arm, so every soldier stood its ground; in the original the twenty patrol types — the majority of the roster — advance, reposition and hunt instead.

member.summary: Works out a burst the way 0x48B9C0 does.
member.param: The AI's combat row.
The held weapon's category.
The weapon's clip size — its config +1608.
The weapon's own burst length — its config +1612.
How far away the tracked aim point is.
The AI's primary view length, which the range is scaled by.
A value in [0, 1).
The argument block's flag, which halves the hit probability.
member.returns: The burst, or one of no rounds for a weapon that does not fire this way.

remarks.para: A weapon whose own burst length differs from its clip size and is above one overrides the clip fraction entirely and is not clamped by the settings row — so a three-round-burst weapon fires three rounds however the row is tuned.

The hit probability is a plain interpolation between the row's minimum-range and maximum-range figures over zero to the primary view length, with the distance clamped to that length first, so a target beyond the cone is scored at the maximum-range figure rather than extrapolated.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.AiCombatParameters
member.summary: The combat block a configured HumanAI carries — +15684 through +15816, plus the two fields that land on the owning body.

remarks.para: sub_406F70 is the only function that writes these, and it applies a conversion on the way in for six of them: four seconds-to-ticks (× 30, truncated toward zero) and four metres-to-units (× 4096). Everything else is copied verbatim. Reproducing the conversion here rather than at each use is what the original does, and it matters — the tick counts are integers, so a delay of 0.33 s is 9 ticks and not 9.9.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.AiEventFilter
member.summary: The filter word a posted AI event carries at +8, deciding which of seven admission tests the receiving AI applies before the event reaches its queue.

remarks.para: Read from 0x450110, HumanAI's handler for the post-event message. The tests are applied in a fixed order and each clears its own bits from the working copy as it runs, which is what lets the enemy/friendly and same-side/other-side pairs ride on shared bits: the engine tests 0x0C and then 0x14, so bit 0x04 participates in both and is consumed by the first.
A word of zero skips every test and is admitted unconditionally — that is the short path 0x450D80 takes for the alarm and idle-animation events it posts itself.
I.G.I. 2's HumanAI_SendEvent applies the same bits, and adds its own above them (0x100 not the originator, 0x200 in view at any distance, 0x400 heard through the level's noise).

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.AiEventQueues
member.summary: The twenty-four per-event-type queues an AI accumulates into, the priority order it drains them in, and the per-type enable mask that gates them.

remarks.para: The layout is fixed by three tables being contiguous inside HumanAI, the same argument that placed the locomotion state table: the queues run +1776..+2064 (24 × a 12-byte list head), the priority order +2076..+2172 (24 ints), the per-type drained counts +2172..+2268 (24 ints) with the order's length at +2268, and the enable mask +2276..+2300 (24 bytes) ending exactly where the pending-action list begins. Every one of those spans is 24 wide, which is the event count.
Three rules together are the whole arbitration (0x44FD50):

list.item: The queues are visited in priority order, not type order. The order holds only the types the script declared, in the order it declared them: AIFunction_SetEventPriority (0x44E0C0) enables a type and appends it the first time it is named, and a type nobody named is never admitted.
At most one event type is dispatched per tick. The first non-empty queue whose position in the order is below the cap runs the script; everything after it is skipped for dispatch.
Every queue is then drained regardless. An event that was not dispatched is discarded, not deferred — so a guard that is busy simply never learns about the shot it heard this tick.

remarks.para: The cap defaults to 24 (anything may dispatch) and otherwise comes from the head pending action's priority at +8. So a running action states how interruptible it is by naming a position in the order, and only events ranked strictly above that position can cut in.

member.name: F:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.AiEventQueues.UnboundedPriorityCap

member.name: F:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.AiEventQueues.RecordPool

member.remarks: Admission takes a record from the free list (0x450520) and drops the event when none is left; the pump returns every record it drains (0x44FE50). So no more than 32 events wait at once, whatever their types.

member.summary: The twenty-eight-byte record one AI event is posted as.
member.param: The event, at +0.

The admission tests to apply, at +8.

remarks.para: is not a priority. It sits where a priority would plausibly go and it is read by 0x450110 as a mask of admission tests; the priority that arbitration uses lives on a pending action, which is a different record. Worth stating because the two structures are one call apart in the pump.

0x450D80, the short helper the engine posts its own alarm and animation events with, writes the type, puts its third argument in and zeroes +16..+24 — leaving and uninitialised stack. member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.AiFreePosition
member.summary: FindFreePosition — sub_48B050 and its acceptance test sub_48B260.

remarks.para: It answers "where should I stand to deal with this target", and it is where the "guards never take cover" complaint is really answered: the original has no cover concept at all, only can I shoot from there.

The search is a breadth-first walk outward from the target's nearest node, testing at most nodes beyond it, and it runs no pathfinding: the direction test is three lookups in the nav graph's precomputed route table.

member.remarks: The queue is a 1024-entry array with a 1024-byte visited map, and a graph declaring 1024 or more slots aborts with a message. No retail graph comes close — the largest declares 400.

member.summary: A guard standing its ground and fighting — 0x48D000, 0x48D080, 0x48D8B0, 0x48D8E0 and 0x48DB10 as one tick machine.

remarks.para: This is the behaviour AIAction_Combat installs for the sniper, Priboi and every one of the twelve GUARD_* types. It does not move: it turns to the target, waits for its stance, sets up a burst, spends it, reloads when the clip runs dry and gives up after the settings row's targeting timeout without sight.
It never shoots. It raises the trigger slot of the input frame and lets the body's own weapon machine turn that into a round, which is what the original does.

remarks.para: The guard's children fire and reload, but the decision is the RPG's own. With a round loaded — or straight after a reload, which forces a shot — it fires, except that after a shot or a stance change it first draws, and below 0.4 swaps between its stand and kneel ticks instead of shooting. With no round it reloads kneeling: from the stand tick 0x48AE70 switches to the kneel tick and runs it at once, so the reload starts on the same tick.
It takes no aim slot on the target record (it never calls sub_4511F0), so the crowding limit that holds back a fifth guard never holds back a rocket.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.AiMovementStep
member.summary: One tick of an AI walking its waypoint queue — 0x451540, and the function that makes a bot move.

remarks.para: The AI steers its soldier through the same 160-byte input frame the player's input sampler produces. It writes three floats into the scratch at HumanAI+15476 — the block the per-tick memsets at the top of every tick — and the per-tick posts it to the owning Human under the channel message id. HumanPlayerInput receives the same frame, and AnimTask and AnimCam sit on the same interface; this is the fourth receiver. It is also the reason a bot moves exactly like the player: identical locomotion, identical integrator, identical animation, different source of the frame.

The three slots used are float 0 (turn), float 1 (pitch) and float 4 (forward, written as a literal 1.0). Everything else in the frame stays zero, which is why an AI never strafes, jumps or fires through this path — those come from actions, not from movement.
The angles are divided by π before they are written (the original multiplies by 0.31830987), so the frame carries a turn as a fraction of a half-turn rather than as radians.

member.name: F:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.AiMovementStep.ArrivalThreshold

member.remarks: A box test, not a radius, and it ignores Z entirely: the original tests |local.x| and |local.y| against this separately, so the accepting region is a square column 0.6 m across of unlimited height. A waypoint directly above or below counts as reached.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.AiNodeOccupancy
member.summary: The per-node occupancy claims the free-position search makes, and the sub-slot positions it hands out — the global record list at 0x57D768, records built by sub_452C60, sub-slots claimed by 0x48B780.

remarks.para: A node is divided into a grid of rows = cols = trunc(radius × 0.5) cells (the radius is the node's authored figure in metres), each cell two metres (8192 units) square. A claim does not count one in its own cell: it stamps a five-by-five kernel round it (sub_452B80 over the table at 0x53CA98) -- 100 on the cell, 50 on the ring, 25 on the rim -- and a cell is taken once it reaches , so one claim takes every cell within two of it. A node whose record says occupants ≥ rows × cols is full and the acceptance test (0x48B260) rejects it outright — which means a node with a radius under four metres holds exactly one soldier: its first claimant takes the centre cell through the no-record arm, and the zero-capacity record then turns everyone else away.

The scan over the grid starts from a different corner each time, driven by a shared round-robin counter (dword_5C8BB8) that increments per acceptance test — it is what fans a squad out over a large node instead of stacking everyone on the same cell.

The claimed cell's world position — cell offset from the grid centre, clamped to ±radius, rotated by the node's authored heading — is what retail writes to HumanAI+16048, and what Follow (0x48C860) and RePosition (0x48C760) actually walk to via sub_4522A0.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.AiPatrolCombat
member.summary: The move-and-fight arm — 0x48ABA0's decision half, i.e. sub_48BFD0 (the action choice) and sub_48BE30 (the evasive decision).

remarks.para: AIAction_Combat dispatches every PATROL_*, SECURITY_PATROL_*, MAFIA_PATROL_* and SPETNAZ_PATROL_* type here — most soldiers in the game — where the twelve GUARD_* types, the sniper and Priboi go to instead. The two arms are genuinely different behaviours and this one is not built on the other: a guard holds its ground, a patrol advances, repositions and hunts.

This class is the chooser only. The four behaviours it selects need the movement stepper and the stance channels, which live on the soldier; keeping the decision pure is what makes it testable against the retail settings rows.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.AiPendingActionList
member.summary: The stack of actions an AI has outstanding, and the one rule that decides what happens to it each tick.

remarks.para: New actions go on at the head (0x4AF910). Before they do, 0x450EE0 ends every action above the first pushable one; that one and everything beneath it stay, suspended, and carry on once what was pushed over them has finished. A pushable combat survives a flashbang's flinch; a non-pushable patrol does not survive combat.
Each tick 0x44FEC0 walks it from the head, and it is stranger than it looks:

list.item: entries without a run function are skipped, but a skipped entry with a non-zero countdown gets it decremented;
the walk stops at the first entry that does have a run function, and runs exactly that one. Nothing after it is looked at.

member.summary: Runs a soldier's archetype behaviour script for real — the 55 AI natives bound to a live soldier, so guard.qsc decides what a guard does rather than the port deciding for it.

remarks.para: The original passes the AI to its natives through four globals: dword_5BDA58 the current AI, 5BDA5C the list the AIAction_* calls append to, 5BDA60 the queue the event is read from and 5BDA64 the dispatch position. That is why no AI native takes the AI as an argument and AIFunction_GetCurrentEventType() has arity zero. This host is those globals: sets them, the script runs, and is the result.

Every native in is registered with the arity and return kind the registrar declares, so a script cannot call one that is missing. The AIAction_* ones record what was asked for rather than performing it, which is exactly what the original does — the action is taken by the pump afterwards (0x450E70 for one, 0x450F10 for several).

member.summary: Every soldier's combat numbers — the original's HumanAIConfig, a 29 × 3 table of (AI type, difficulty) rows read out of common/ai/settings.qsc.

remarks.para: sub_406DF0 creates the container, clears 348 bytes of pointers at +36 — 29 types × 3 difficulties — runs the script, files each declared item at difficulty + 3 * aiType, and then fills every slot the script left empty with an item carrying the constructor's own defaults. The difficulty in force is the player profile's, not the AI's — sub_406F70 reads it once per configured HumanAI.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1GuardScript
member.summary: Reads a Project I.G.I. guard's orders off its own script, MISSION:AI/<mind id>.qsc.

remarks.para: A guard's script is one event switch, run each time its mind is told something: on AIEVENT_CREATE it sets the guard's alarm, gunner and view; on AIEVENT_IDLE it sends it on its patrol (AIAction_Patrol), and on AIEVENT_ALARMON on another, where it has one; anything else goes to AIFunction_DefaultHandler. The script is run here for those three events in a namespace of the game's own constants (), with every native it calls recorded rather than done, and the level's own variables read as nought -- a quiet level -- so what it would have the guard do from the start is what it says.
A script that cannot run so -- one that faults, or waits on the level to say something first -- gives no orders, and the guard does as its kind does.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi
member.content: The action stack: the script's dispatch, installing what it produced, and each action's start, run and end functions.
The per-tick behaviours the actions install: the patrol walker, the activate walk, panic, a look at an event, a fall, a stun and scripted fire.
The combat action: the arm the AI type selects, the input frame it writes, the shared target record, and the guard arm's tick.
member.summary: One soldier's AI runtime — the parts of HumanAI the port has read, joined up and driving a body.

remarks.para: This is the integration of what is settled about the original's AI: the nav graph and its precomputed route table, the event pump's arbitration, the two view cones, the detection cascade's three gates and the patrol step machine and waypoint steering. Every rule and constant here is read; what is not yet read is the QVM behaviour script that decides which action to take, so the choice between patrolling and engaging is made here directly rather than by running guard.qsc.

Speed comes from the animation's own root motion, which is how this engine moves a human at all (M8) — so a soldier covers exactly the ground its walk clip covers, and no invented speed constant appears anywhere in this class.

What is faithful: the cones and their alert-selected ranges, the detection phase gate and rate limits, the 0.3 m box arrival test, the route table being followed one step at a time with no A*, the walk-versus-run gait, the idle fallback, and strict occlusion by the port's world-only sight cast. Script events/actions, authored patrol routes, combat target sharing, and hearing are handled by the same facade so they consume the same HumanAI state rather than a second coarse activity model.

Like its IGI 2 sibling the class is split by facet, all over the one HumanAI state: this file holds the wiring and the state, and .Perception, .Actions, .Behaviours, .Routing, .Movement, .Combat, .PatrolCombat, .Life and .Diagnostics the rest.

member.content: Diagnostics for the debug overlay and the scenario traces, for diffing the port against the retail probe log.
A soldier's tick, its death and its respawn.
The body the AI's frame drives: the turn and pitch it writes, the recoil it carries, and the move on the clip's root motion at the graph's height.
The move-and-fight arm the PATROL_* types and the named characters fight with — 0x48ABA0 and the behaviours it installs.
What a soldier senses: the detection scan, its view cones and eye, and the events it hears and is sent.
Graph routing: the movement queue the planner builds and the walker steps, door hops, and the combat free-position search.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.RemoveAlarmActions
member.summary: Ends the actions the alarm is meant to have installed — AIFunction_RemoveAlarmActions (0x44DBC0), which guard.qsc calls on ALARMOFF.
member.remarks: The original ends every action whose priority equals the word at HumanAI+2108. That word is the ninth entry of the priority order — an event type — compared against a priority position, so it ends what the event at that position installed, not the alarm run. With the archetypes' order, the ninth entry is GUNSHOT (16) and position 16 is EXPLOSION; an alarm run installed from COMBAT carries on after the alarm is switched off. Reproduced as it is.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.ApplyActions(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.AiProducedAction})
member.summary: Installs whatever the archetype script asked for on the last dispatch.
member.param: The produced actions, in script order.

remarks.para: The original hands one produced action to 0x450E70 and several to 0x450F10, and both do the same three things. First 0x450EE0 ends every action above the first pushable one on the stack. Then each produced action goes on at the head and its start function runs.

The produced list is built in script order (each AIAction_* appends at the tail through 0x450E10 -> 0x4AF8F0), and 0x450F10 walks it from the TAIL back, adding each to the head (0x4AF910). So the FIRST action the script named ends up on top and runs first: a guard's COMBAT branch, Activate(alarm trigger) then Combat, runs to the alarm and fights after. Installing in script order had the fight on top, and a guard that saw you never went for the alarm.

Every action takes the flag word of the first one walked -- the LAST the script named. A start that finishes its own action (SetCombat posts COMBAT; a refused Activate never begins) leaves nothing on the stack.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.RunActivate
member.summary: The Activate per-tick (0x48E7D0): walk to the panel's node, press on arrival, release the claims. Retail picks the gait from the action's run flag and presses through input channel 4 -- the port walks its ordinary route and invokes the activation directly; both are recorded stand-ins.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.RunPanicking
member.summary: The RunPanicking per-tick: run to the chosen node, and end on arrival.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.RunPatrolCommand(System.Int32)
member.summary: Runs one tick of the current patrol command — the human walker 0x48E920.

remarks.para: The order is the walker's: the crouch flag and the gait are applied first and unconditionally, because both outlive the command that set them, and only then does the switch run. A command that reports itself finished advances the cursor and clears the deadline; a kind the walker has no arm for returns without advancing, which is how a wedges a human patrol — reproduced rather than smoothed over.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.RunScriptedFire
member.summary: One tick of FireAtNode / FireAtTask — 0x48ECC0 / 0x48EE00.
member.remarks: The time runs down first and ends the action. An empty clip reloads through the input slot and fires nothing that tick, or refills at once and sets the next burst up afresh. A burst is set up (0x48B9C0, at full accuracy) the first tick there is none, then -- once the wait armed after the last burst has run out, and with no turning while it does -- fired through combat's own fire child (0x48D8E0); its end arms the wait again.

member.summary: The close-combat blow at its clip's hit frame (event 12) — Soldier_MeleeUpdate (0x45B530).
member.param: Receives the row's damage factor when the blow lands.
member.returns: when it lands on the soldier's target.
member.remarks: The level's stream is drawn first, every time: a draw over the row's chance (+15768) misses. A hit needs a target, and does the row's damage (+15772) through the target's punch handler. A class whose entry latches the blow done (the pistol soldier's +3353) never reaches the draw.

member.name: P:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.IsMovingInCombat
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the soldier is walking a combat route this tick.
member.remarks: True whenever the move-and-fight arm stepped the soldier — advancing on a target, repositioning, or hunting a lost one while it watches. The renderer plays the WALK clip for it, because the walk clip's own root motion is what the next tick's moves by; playing the fire pose instead (as the raw action would, since a hunting soldier's action is LookForTarget most ticks) leaves the clip with no motion and the chase never travels.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.EnterCombat

member.remarks: Every path into combat comes through here, and that matters: once the machine ends — a targeting timeout, or a target with no detection slot — its phase is and every later tick returns "ended" at once. Re-arming only on the scripted path left a soldier that engaged a second way permanently unable to fight, which reads exactly as a guard that sees you and does nothing. 0x48D000 arms it when the action is taken, which is what this is.

member.name: P:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.IsWalking
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the soldier is walking rather than running.
member.remarks: Three sources name the gait, mirroring the retail per-ticks that call the walk/run setters (sub_4525E0/sub_452660) every tick: an AIAction_Activate's run argument (0x48E7D0), the patrol cursor's gait flag set by (0x48E920), and AIAction_RunToNode against AIAction_WalkToNode. Only the action that runs sets it, so a patrol suspended under a fight does not choose the fight's gait.

member.name: P:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.WalkGait
member.summary: Gets the gait the body read this tick: the run byte at Human+3328, set for walking.

remarks.para: is what the running action asks for; this is what the body does. The soldier's create (0x45CC50) sets the byte, and only a press of input slot 20 -- the AI's channel 0 -- flips it, in 0x45D080 AFTER the body machine (0x4EC1E0) has read it. The walk and run setters (0x4525E0, 0x452660) press it when it is wrong for the gait. Their callers: the patrol's start (0x48E8C0, walk), the patrol runner (0x48E920, from the cursor's gait flag BEFORE the command runs -- the flag a new cursor starts with is walk, 0x4537E0), Activate (0x48E7D0), Move To Event (0x48E020), Walk/Run To Node (0x48EBF0/0x48EC50) and Combat - Follow (0x48C860, run).

So a patrol that opens on a RunTo walks two ticks first: its first tick sets the walk gait from the new cursor, its second presses for the run, and the body reads the old byte on that tick too. Probed on mission 4: squad member 400 went state 3 (walk), 3, then 2 (run), slot 20 set on the second tick and the byte clear from the third; walking patrols, whose byte was right from the start, never pressed.

member.remarks: The patrol walker (0x48E920) writes the crouch channel on every tick it runs, and the channel block is cleared at the start of every tick, so the crouch lasts only while the patrol is running.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.Respawned(OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d,System.Single,System.Func{OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi,OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.AiCombatWeaponState})

The authored soldier heading.
Reads the respawned brain's weapon state. The owner is supplied so renderer callbacks cannot retain the dead brain while querying mounted-gun state.
member.returns: A new brain with the same level wiring and reset AI execution state.
member.remarks: IGI1's 0x488000/0x488040 path constructs the whole stored child subtree again. A new is the managed equivalent: CREATE will run again on its first tick, while immutable level services (graph, scripts, collision queries and combat row) are reattached here. The caller must assign a unique before registering the new brain alongside retained corpses, and rebind view-tracking callbacks to its new rendered body.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.TickDeadAi(System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: A dead soldier's HumanAI tick, before its body's: once the death clip has run (Human+828, set by 0x45C740 the tick after the clip ends), 0x44F410 lets go of the alarm panel's claim handles and its node cell, so a guard shot on its way to the alarm leaves it for the next one only once the body lies still. It then counts the body's stay down, and says when the body leaves the world.
member.param: Whether the last rendered frame drew the body: Human_DrawHandler (0x45F280) stamps Human+0x7C4 with the render count when its frustum sphere (0x4D06C0) lets the body through, and the render count goes up after the draw, so "drawn by the last render" is retail's renders - stamp <= 1. A body never drawn (stamp −1) counts as not drawn.
Whether the soldier is a GuardGenerator's, whose body leaves in sight or not.
member.returns: Whether the body leaves the world on this tick (0x4609A0).
member.remarks: HumanAI+0x3E10 starts at 300 (0x44F060, its only writer besides the countdown) and runs down one a tick from the first tick the dead Human is settled, past nought: clip ends on tick E, the count runs E+1..E+301, and from E+302 the body leaves on the first tick the last render did not draw it -- a corpse in view stays, one out of view goes. Every soldier's body does this, not only a generator's; a generator's goes on E+302 regardless.

member.name: P:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.HasLeftWorld
member.summary: Gets whether the dead body has left the world (0x4609A0 cleared Human+3318): nothing ticks, draws or meets it.

member.name: F:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.BodyStayTicks
member.summary: HumanAI+0x3E10's start: the ticks a settled body stays before it may leave the world (0x44F060 writes 300).

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.TickDeadBody(OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3f,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Steps a dead body for one tick — the death state's per-tick (0x45C700) joined to the soldier update's ordinary root-motion move and ground query (0x45D080).
member.param: What the death clip's own root-motion track moved this tick, in the body's model space. The soldier update rotates exactly this into world space and hands it to the movement integrator.
Whether the death clip ended this tick, after which the corpse stops sliding.

remarks.para: Three things move a corpse, and all three are here: the clip's root motion, the solver's corrective velocity, and the ground query snapping the body onto whatever is under it. Nothing else does — the solver's own output is purely horizontal (its vertical component is forced to zero before the arithmetic starts), so a body falls because its death clip's root track goes down and the ground catches it.

A soldier with no ground query keeps the Z its clip gives it, which is the same fallback the living path takes. When a ground service exists but has no support for a placed upper floor, the last feet height is retained and the renderer's root sample supplies the visible fall pose.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.Tick(System.Int32,OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d,System.Double,System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.Nullable{OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d},System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.Double)
member.summary: Runs one 30 Hz tick.
member.param: The engine tick counter, which the detection phase gate keys off.
The enemy's world position — the player's eye.

How far the soldier's current animation moves it this tick along its own forward axis, in engine units — signed, so a clip that steps back moves the soldier back. The engine moves a human by its clip's root motion and nothing else, so this is the only speed source.
Whether an alarm the soldier watches is sounding.
Whether that alarm sounded on the preceding tick, for the falling-edge event.

Whether the enemy is still a valid target. A dead enemy is not: the detection scan (0x489750) unregisters a human that reports itself invalid, so the soldier loses it and leaves combat instead of firing at the corpse. reproduces that.
The enemy task's position — its feet, which is what combat aims at (sub_451380 raises it 0.5 m, 0.25 m crouched). Defaults to when the caller has no body.
Whether the enemy is crouching, which halves the aim raise.
The clip's root motion along the body's own right axis, in engine units.

Whether the fed enemy is another soldier rather than the player. The player is only a target to a hostile team, so a friendly never registers it; another soldier is a target to any soldier whose team differs from the enemy's own, regardless of the player relationship.

member.summary: Gets the yaw the weapon's kick still holds the body off its heading by -- the view's +308.
member.remarks: 0x4610C0 builds the body's matrix from the heading plus this (Human+1288 = +1292 + view+308), so the kick turns the body, its movement and its eye, and the AI's next turn measures against it.

member.name: P:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.RecoilPitch
member.summary: Gets the pitch the weapon's kick still holds the view off -- the view's +296, added in 0x464800.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.SettleRecoil
member.summary: Folds the last round's kick into the recoil the view carries -- 0x462E50, every tick, after the turn and move.
member.remarks: Each offset becomes (kick + offset) x 0.9, so a burst climbs and a pause lets it settle. The kick is the one the weapon returned on the PREVIOUS tick: the gun fires after this, and its kick waits in the fire message for the next tick's pass. So a soldier's AI, which runs before its body, measures its turn against the recoil as it was when it last fired. Fitted on mission 4's squad member 405 to a millionth of a radian over a whole burst.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.SetGroundQuery(OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.GroundQuery)
member.summary: Gives the soldier a ground query, so it walks on the terrain instead of interpolating between graph nodes.
member.param: The query, or to fall back to linear interpolation along the leg.

remarks.para: In the original the AI steers the soldier through the player's own input frame (0x451540), which makes the Human task run the same movement integrator as the player (0x4614B0), including its ground query (0x462390). So a soldier's height comes from the terrain (or whatever placed object it stands on), not from the graph.

Probing the retail game confirms soldiers run the integrator with wallEnable=0 objEnable=1 humanEnable=0: object collision and ground query but no wall sweep. The nav graph itself keeps soldiers on walkable paths; wall collision is not needed.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.FaceNode(System.Int32)
member.summary: A patrol's LookAtNode — 0x452580, the look-at entry into the turn.
member.returns: once facing the node within 3 degrees.
member.remarks: The look-at entry sets the turn clamp to 0.0259 rad of input per tick (0x3CD4629B), so a patrol turns to look at a node at about 24 degrees a second rather than snapping to it; the walk and the combat turns set it back to pi.

member.summary: Where the target really is, raised to where the combat code aims — sub_451380.
member.remarks: The guard's turn to an unseen target and every burst's aim point read the target task's own position (0.5 m up, 0.25 m crouched), not the shared record the rest of combat reads; only the distance, and a knife guard's turn, use the record.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.RunSharedSubAction(OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d,OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.AiCombatWeaponState)

The held weapon's state this tick.

member.name: F:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.FollowFireCosine
member.summary: The cosine a following patrol fires within — 0x48C860's 0.96, a 16.3° cone.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.FacesForFollowFire(OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d)
member.summary: Whether the record point lies inside the running fire cone — 0x48C860.
member.param: The shared record's point: the target's origin raised (0x451380).
member.remarks: The test is three-dimensional: the view's forward (the run levels the view, 0x451540) against the direction from the AI's view position (its feet) to the record point, which stands about a metre and a half over them. So the cone narrows with the height difference, and a target a few metres off is above it: a running patrol holds its fire until it is clear of the target, and only fires at range.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.HeadFor(System.Int32)
member.summary: Sets a destination, but only when it is a new one.
member.param: Where to head.
member.remarks: clears the route and re-anchors the leg origin every time it is called, so a combat behaviour that asks for the same destination on every tick would restart the leg forever and the soldier would never actually travel. The original sets the destination once (HumanAI+15848) and the movement stepper walks the queue; this keeps that shape.

member.name: F:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.FreePositionArrivalInUnits
member.summary: How close to the claimed sub-slot counts as standing on it — half a metre.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.AdvanceInCombat
member.summary: Steps the soldier along its combat route, the same walk the patrol path uses.
member.remarks: The move-and-fight arm sets a Follow/RePosition destination but the original then walks to it — the AI steers its Human through the input frame and the body's mover carries it. Without this the port set a destination it never travelled, which is exactly "guards engage but don't chase". The distance covered is the run clip's own root motion (M8), so no speed is invented. Once the route delivers the body to the node, the walk finishes at the claimed sub-slot inside it — retail's sub_4522A0 against the position at HumanAI+16048.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.LiveTargetFeet(OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d)
member.summary: Where the target human stands now, seen or not -- what 0x451380 reads (its +32).
member.param: The point to use when no human is tracked as the target.
member.remarks: The shared record's copy (+272) is refreshed only while the target is seen or an event arrives (0x48A920); the node lookup 0x4530A0 and the free-position search 0x48B050 both call 0x451380 instead, which reads the target human itself. Mission 4's guard 411 lost sight of the squad for 36 ticks and its node still moved from 13 to 14 halfway through.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.CombatDistance(OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d)
member.summary: The combat action's distance to its target -- 0x48A920's +16 of the action block.
member.param: The shared record's position, as the port keeps it: the target's feet.
member.remarks: Measured from the soldier's own origin (Human+32) to the record's point, which 0x451380 stored as the target's origin raised half a metre (a quarter crouched). Close combat, the lie-down range, the walk toward the target and the grenade window all compare against it.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.TrackTargetNode(OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d)
member.summary: 0x48A920's tracking of the node nearest the target -- HumanAI+15852 and +15856.
member.param: Where the target is.

member.name: F:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.SightObstructionTolerance
member.summary: The fraction of the eye-to-mark segment beyond which an object contact no longer hides the target — 0x489B20's fraction >= 0.79000002.
member.remarks: Terrain always blocks (0x4CE410 forces its fraction to zero). An object — a crate, a wall, a building, most of what the levels are made of — hides the target only when it is nearer than this, so cover pressed up against the target leaves it visible.

member.name: F:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.DetectionRaiseStandingInUnits
member.summary: How far above its feet a standing human reports itself to detection — the Z offset the descriptor handler adds in sub_465820: 2826.24 units (0.69 m), stored as the dwords 0xE147AE14 and 0x40A6147A.
member.remarks: Vision does not test the target's eye. The candidate describes itself for the sweep (sub_45FE30) as its position plus this raise — mid-body — and the cone test, the sight ray and the stored distance all take that one point. Testing the eye let a guard acquire a player whose head cleared a sill while retail's waist-height mark stayed hidden.

member.name: F:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.DetectionRaiseCrouchedInUnits
member.summary: The crouched raise — sub_465820's other constant, 1433.6 units (0.35 m), the dwords 0x66666666 and 0x40966666.

member.name: F:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.HumanOriginStandingInUnits
member.summary: How far above its feet a standing human's origin (Human+32) is — 0.97 m.
member.remarks: The port keeps a human's position at its feet; IGI.exe keeps it at the model origin, which its ground query stands at the node or ground height plus the root bone's height (0x462390 via sub_48A340). Measured on the retail game: the player landed at 0.97 m over the port's ground at the mission-1 spawn, and guard 2003's origin matches the port's drawn origin (the soldier model's lowest vertex is 0.970 m below it) to the centimetre.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.HearGunshot(OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Delivers a gunshot the soldier might hear — posts if it is in earshot.
member.param: Where the shot was fired, in engine units.
Whether the weapon is silenced, which cuts the audible range to a thirtieth.
member.returns: when the shot was within earshot and an event was queued.

remarks.para: The ranges are the two constants the AI module registers: (30 m) and (1 m) — a silenced weapon is worth carrying because it is heard a thirtieth as far. The event carries the shot's position, so a script can ask AIFunction_GetEventDistance, and it is pumped on the soldier's next tick like any other event — so a guard already busy with a higher-priority event this tick never learns of the shot, which is the original's discard-not-defer rule.

Recorded as a delivery, not a reaction. What a guard does about a heard shot is its archetype script's AIEVENT_GUNSHOT branch; this only puts the event where the script can see it. A projectile passing close to the head is a separate delivery, modelled by .

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.GoTo(System.Int32,System.Nullable{OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Plans a walk to a graph node — 0x4518E0.
member.param: The destination node id.
An exact point to finish at inside the destination node, or for its centre.
Whether the walk claims its destination's cell first (0x4518E0's fourth argument), as the patrol walker, WalkToNode, RunToNode and MoveToEvent do.
member.returns: when the whole route was planned.

remarks.para: The queue is of points, not nodes. Where a hop leaves a node the walker aims for the edge of that node's square on the line to the next one, and where it arrives, for the edge it crosses (0x4520C0); the destination's own centre — or the exact point, when it lies inside the node — is last. So a soldier cuts across a node's square instead of touching every centre.

It starts from the current node when the soldier is standing in it. Otherwise it first walks back into a node: the current one, or the next node of the old queue when the soldier is already inside that, or when that one is nearer the destination by the route's cost than the current node is by distance.
A route that breaks off ("Error in graph %d routenet") keeps what was built and the goal, as the original does, and the walk carries on along it.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.StepTowardsNode(System.Int32)
member.summary: The walk to a node that the patrol walker, the go-to actions, the alarm run and panic share — 0x4522A0 into 0x4518E0.
member.returns: on the tick the walk ends.
member.remarks: It plans only when the goal changes, and walks the queue otherwise, so a soldier pushed off its line does not re-plan. A plan that fails returns before stepping; the goal is then set, and on the next tick the soldier walks whatever part of the route was built and ends when it runs out.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.Advance
member.summary: Walks the movement queue for one tick — the planner's stepping loop around 0x451540.
member.returns: once the queue is empty: the walk is over.

remarks.para: Reaching a waypoint (within 0.3 m on both of the body's horizontal axes, height ignored) pops it, makes its node the current one and steps the next waypoint in the same tick (while (sub_451540(ai) == 0)), so a walker never pauses at an intermediate point. Only an empty queue ends the walk, and that also clears the goal.
The walker only writes the frame: the turn, a level view and forward. The body turns and moves after it, on its own clip — see .

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi.HoldForDoor(OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d)
member.summary: A door hop's hold — the door branch of 0x451540.
member.returns: while the soldier waits on the door rather than walking.
member.remarks: The walker finds the nearest door once per hop and acts on its state: 1 (closed) and 3 (closing) — open it with the player's own use (sub_447DA0) and hold; 2 (moving) — "Waiting for door to open", hold; 0 (open) — walk through. Holding turns to the waypoint at the 2-degree door tolerance.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.ISoldierPresenter.FollowPlayerBody(OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d,System.Single,System.Int32,System.Boolean,OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.PlayerBodyPose@)
member.summary: Walks the third-person body with the player, in the clip the player's own legs are in.
member.param: Where the player is standing, in engine units — PlayerBody.Position.
Which way the body faces, in radians — the player's yaw.
The clip the player's is playing, or for the states that name none.
Whether that state's table entry loops.
The half of the body the legs' clip does not drive — the weapon's torso animation and where the player is looking. See .

remarks.para: Called on the simulation tick, not on the frame. The body's clip advances one authoring frame per and the player's animator advances one per tick, so stepping it here — and only here — is what keeps the two in phase without any clock being copied between them: the same state entered on the same tick starts the same clip at the same zero. Step it from the draw instead and a display slower than 30 Hz walks the legs at less than the speed the body is actually travelling, which is a character skating along the ground.
The placement is the ordinary one a soldier gets — the task position lifted by the clip's own root height (PlayerBodyPlacement) — so a crouch sits where a crouching guard sits.
is a gamma, not the player's yaw: the two run opposite ways, and the caller negates. See the call site in DesktopGame.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.ISoldierPresenter.Tick(OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d,System.Boolean,System.Nullable{OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Advances every soldier's animation by one tick and re-skins the groups.

remarks.para: Nothing advanced a soldier's rig before this existed, so every guard in the level stood frozen on the first frame of its stand animation — which reads as a default A-pose. Soldiers are grouped by (model, skeleton, animation) and share one skinned mesh, so ticking the group's first soldier and re-skinning from its pose animates the whole group: they run the same clip from the same start, so they share a pose by construction.

The device's meshes are immutable, so this destroys and re-uploads. There are only a handful of groups in a level, so it is a few uploads a tick — worth replacing with a dynamic vertex buffer, but not worth leaving the guards frozen for.

member.param: The enemy's eye position, which the view cones are tested against.

Whether the enemy is still a target. A dead player is not: the detection scan (0x489750) unregisters a human that reports itself invalid, so the guards lose it and stop firing at the corpse — passing reproduces that.
The enemy task's position — its feet, what combat aims at (sub_451380). Defaults to when the caller has no body to speak of.
Whether the enemy is crouching, which halves the aim raise.

member.param: The list to fill; cleared first.

remarks.para: A read-only projection rather than access to the soldiers themselves. The inspector runs on the far side of an interface that must not see gameplay types, and a panel holding a live SoldierView across a mission change would be holding a corpse the loader had forgotten about. Everything the panel needs is copied out here, once per frame it draws.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.SoldierContext.Stand(OpenIGI.Game.Player.HumanSoldierTask,OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.SoldierModelGroup,OpenIGI.Game.World.IGroundHeightField,OpenIGI.Game.World.WorldRayCast)
member.summary: Puts a soldier's feet on whatever is under its declared position.

remarks.para: In the original the level's declared Position is only where a soldier starts: its update runs the same movement integrator as the player's, whose ground pass (0x462390) snaps the body onto the surface below within the first ticks. The port does not tick soldiers yet, so a body drawn with its skeleton root at the declared height stands buried to the waist wherever the position was authored at floor level.

This reproduces the settled state, not the mechanism: probe down from half a metre above the declared position — placed objects first, terrain as the fallback, highest surface wins — and stand the skin's lowest vertex on it. The original's own foot reference is 0x48A340's bone-0-plus-Human+1300 offset, and the +1300 term is still unread, so the mesh's own extent is the honest stand-in. A recorded divergence, retired with the soldier update.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.SoldierContext.SnapToGround(System.Double,System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: The collision surface under a point, in world units — placed objects first, terrain second.
member.param: The point's X, in world units.
Its Y.
The feet the query starts from; returned unchanged when nothing is under them.
member.returns: The highest floor within the probe, or if none.
member.remarks: The same query runs, without the mesh lift — for grounding a live soldier's feet each frame. It chooses the highest support in the probe and can therefore lower a soldier whose authored spawn is slightly above the terrain, as well as lift one authored just below its floor.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.SoldierContext.OccupantOrigin(OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Player.SoldierView)
member.summary: The point an area counts a soldier at: its origin, Human+32, not its feet.

remarks.para: The human criteria callbacks an AreaActivate runs (0x460A10 for CRITERIA_HUMAN%d, 0x460A70 for CRITERIA_HUMAN) hand the box test 0x5042B0 each registered human's +32. For a soldier that is the ground its AI stood it on plus the clip's root height (0x462390 adds Human+1300, ): about 0.95 m above the feet standing.

Counting the feet dropped mission 4's running squad out of "Team one stop 1" (AreaActivate_150), whose floor is 0.25 m above the ground they cross. Retail's squad fills it at tick 3818 and opens the med-warehouse guards (ConditionalContainer_302) on them; the port's never did, so the squad reached its stops unopposed where retail's is fighting by tick 4548.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.SoldierDamage.DropVelocity(OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d,OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d)
member.summary: What a gun leaves a dying hand with: the body's own motion plus a share of the round's knock.
member.param: The body's motion, units per tick, in world space.
The killing round's line.
member.returns: The launch velocity, units per tick.
member.remarks: The grip opens as the round lands, so the gun keeps what the body was doing and takes a small push along the shot -- sixty centimetres a second, a sideways stumble rather than a throw -- with a little lift from the arm flinching. Only the realistic drop reads it; the original's ignores it.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.SoldierDamage.Die(OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Player.SoldierView,OpenIGI.Game.Player.HumanHit,OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d,OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d,OpenIGI.Game.Weapons.WeaponCategory,OpenIGI.Game.Player.SoldierDeathMode)
member.summary: Puts a soldier into the general death state — 0x45C440, joined up.

remarks.para: Four things happen here and every one of them is read. The body turns to the round (0x45DAA0); the death animation is chosen from the killing weapon's category, the zone struck and which way the round came (); the fall solver fans its nine rays and returns the corrective velocity (); and the brain is told, so it steps the body every tick from then on instead of freezing it.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.SoldierDamage.TryDieOfPendingRound(OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Player.SoldierView)
member.summary: Enters the death state a marched round left a soldier in, on the update after it struck.
member.param: The soldier updating.
member.returns: Whether a round had killed it.
member.remarks: The machine sees the dead bit the killing round set and enters the death state (0x45C440). The entry only starts the clip: the death state's per-tick (0x45C700), which moves the body, runs from the next tick.

member.param: The soldier.
The entry.
The pass's start.
The pass's end.
The firing weapon.
The round's damage factor.
The soldier that fired, or .
member.remarks: The blood first (0x45F94A), then the damage handler (0x45D3C0): an invulnerable body (the mission 4 squad's SetInvulnerability(TRUE)) takes the round and nothing else.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.SoldierDamage.TakeRound(OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Player.SoldierView,OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1WeaponHit)
member.summary: A round or a blade on a soldier, whoever fired it: HumanSoldier's WeaponHit, 0x45D3C0.

remarks.para: Invulnerability (HumanAI+15036) skips the whole damage block -- the round still meets the body, it just does nothing; instant death disabled (+15037) makes a head or neck hit take the plain damage. The blood follows the damage (0x45D45C), then the death or the flinch and the grunt, and the blade's own sound for a knife.
Whatever the round did, the brain is told last: the TAKINGDAMAGE event (type 15) goes out at 0x45D577 to an invulnerable soldier as much as to a wounded one.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.SoldierDamage.TakePunch(OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Player.SoldierView,OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Player.SoldierView,System.Single)

member.param: The soldier struck.
The soldier who struck.
The attacker's close-combat damage.
member.remarks: The blow lands on the back (zone 14) when the attacker stands behind the struck soldier's facing, else on the front (zone 13), scaled by that zone's multiplier. Short of the soldier's maximum it reacts as to a round; at it the soldier crumples away from the attacker. Either way the brain is told who hit it, an invulnerable one too.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.SoldierGunShotRounds.TryShootAiRound(OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d,OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d,System.Single,OpenIGI.Game.Weapons.WeaponType,OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Player.SoldierView,System.Nullable{OpenIGI.Game.World.WorldRayHit},OpenIGI.Game.Player.HumanHit@)
member.summary: Offers an AI-fired round to the soldiers and scores it against the nearest one it meets. This is the NPC-vs-NPC counterpart to TryShoot: a guard's round can strike a friendly, and a friendly's can strike a guard, so Harrison's team at the gate trades fire with the guards instead of only ever being aimed at the player.
member.param: Where the round starts, in world units.
Where the round stops.
The firing AI's chance the round is on target (its Human+1236). Retail rolls it only against the player, so a soldier the round meets never consults it; it is kept for the callers' symmetry.
The firing weapon, whose damage factor and category apply on a hit.
The soldier that fired; its own body is never offered the round.
The nearest world surface ahead, when the world blocks the ray; a soldier behind it is never offered the round (the wall already took it). when no surface stopped it.
The soldier struck, when one is.
member.returns: when a soldier consumed the round (damaged, or a same-team/invulnerable body the round met and stopped at); when it met nobody and flies on.
member.remarks: The damage is applied here, exactly as in TryShoot. The Human's evaluate (0x45E3E0) decides each body the round meets, nearest first: one on the shooter's own side (Human+252) lets it pass through to the next, any other takes it -- with no probability roll, which retail makes only for the player. Scripted invulnerability (500.qvm sets SetInvulnerability(TRUE) on the friendly squad, so they cannot die) makes the round meet the body but do nothing; the body is still a physical obstacle that consumes it.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.SoldierGunShotRounds.HearRoundsPassing(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Weapons.GunShotRound},OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Player.SoldierView)
member.summary: Offers a task's rounds to every human they pass, before the march: 0x4606F0 for each human, with 0x47B290's points.

remarks.para: A human on the shooter's side, or the shooter, hears nothing. For any other, each round whose line passes within four metres of the human's origin gives the nearest point on it; the point is broadcast as GUNSHOTMISS with radius two metres, filter 0x46 and the shooter's side, and every AI on another side within two metres of it takes it. The line is the round's whole range, cast or not, so a body the round will strike hears it pass as well.
The player hears its own whizz (gunshotmiss) instead; that is the host's.

member.summary: The noises the level's soldiers hear: gunshots, blasts, impacts, steps, grenades and rounds going by, each broadcast to every human on the level's list and weighed by the listening brain.
member.remarks: The engine's broadcast (0x450CE0) sends one record to every human, each taking it in its own handler. member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.SoldierPlayerBody.HideFollowing
member.summary: Stops following the player — the view has gone back inside their head.

remarks.para: And gives the rig back. The torso clip on bone 1 and the aim bend belong to the follow and to nothing else: while the player is on a ladder, at a keypad, cutting a wire or dead, an authored full-body clip owns the whole character, and a weapon stance left in its shoulders replaces the half of that clip above the waist. and release it too, so no ordering between this and them can leave the override behind — but doing it here as well is what makes the invariant a property of the follow rather than of a list of call sites.
Cheap to repeat: this is called on every tick the follow is not running, and both releases return at once when there is nothing to release.

member.remarks: The body renderer adds the current root Z above the task, while the third-person camera normally follows the task itself. member.summary: Scores a guard's round on the player's own body — its skinned collision mesh.
member.param: Where the round starts, in world units.
Where it stops.
The player's feet, in world units.
Which way the player faces, in radians.
The contact, when there is one.
member.returns: when the round misses the player's body, or no body is loaded.
member.remarks: The original resolves a shot at the player exactly as at a soldier — against the human's skinned collision mesh — so a round through a limb scores that limb (×0.5–0.75), not the torso. The port had cast at a 0.55 m cylinder and scored every hit as the trunk, which made the player both a fatter target and one that took maximum damage from every round. This poses the player's own (otherwise idle) third-person body at the live position and heading and traces the real mesh.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.SoldierSightQueries.HasLineOfSight(OpenIGI.Game.World.WorldTraceCast,OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d,OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d,System.Double,OpenIGI.Engine.Tasks.GameTask,System.Func{OpenIGI.Engine.Tasks.GameTask,System.Boolean})
member.summary: Whether the eye can see a point, treating glass and fences as non-occluding.
member.param: The world trace.
The eye.
The point looked at.
How far along the eye-to-point segment, as a fraction, an object contact has to be before it stops counting as cover. 1 makes every contact block.

remarks.para: A cast returns only its NEAREST contact, so a single probe would stop at a chain-link fence and never notice a solid wall right behind it. This steps the ray past each transparent surface (glass, wire) and keeps looking, so a guard behind a fence is seen but one behind the wall the fence stands in front of is not. See .

Terrain always blocks. An object contact blocks only nearer than the tolerance: the AI's sight ray (0x489B20) is visible when 0x4CE410 reports no contact or the contact's segment fraction is at least 0.79, and 0x4CE410 forces the fraction to zero for a terrain hit.

member.param: The viewer itself, when it has a body the ray would otherwise meet -- a vehicle.
Whether an object the ray meets answers the detection ray that it is not in the way: a stationary gun does, for a ray from or to the human on it (0x4752B0).
member.returns: when the line is clear.

remarks.para: 0x489B20 casts through 0x4CE410, which visits every dynamic object along the whole segment (message 8, 0x4C8130) before it consults static geometry -- so a wall between does not spare anyone. The human filter it hands the visit (0x42FC50) admits every human but the looker and the target. A human it admits is tested by 0x45F580: the segment against a sphere of the model's bound (Human+160) about the origin (Human+32), the perpendicular distance from the line and the two boxes' overlap. On a hit 0x45F800 rebuilds the palette (0x45F240).

Probed on mission 4: squad member 404 ran beside 405, and every 12 ticks guard 411's ray to 405 refreshed 404 -- never 405 itself. 404's ray to 411 at tick 4544 refreshed bystander 403, whose eye then turned south and saw guards 409 and 410 three ticks later.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.SoldierSimulation
member.summary: The level's soldiers as the game runs them: their brains, their health and weapons, what they hear and see, and the player's own body where it is a soldier's.

remarks.para: What draws them is SoldierRenderer, which holds one of these and reads it; this holds nothing it draws. The soldiers are walked through , group by group in the order the level made them, which is the order their brains tick in.

This is the coordinator: it runs each soldier's update in the original's order and hands the parts of it to the pieces that own them -- the brains' making (), what the soldiers see () and hear (), their weapons () and rounds (), what hits do to them () and the generators that replace them (). All of them share one , so every part reads the same roster, brains and random stream.

member.content: Who is noticing the player, as a heads-up display marks them.

How the soldiers are wired to the level and the game around them: the services they cast against, the sinks their sounds, deaths and rounds go to, and the face the rest of the game reads them through -- each of which hands on to the part that owns it.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.SoldierSimulation.AttachTo(OpenIGI.Game.World.LevelUpdateWalker)
member.summary: Puts the soldiers, their guard generators, the doors and the alarm controls into the level's walk.
member.param: The level walk.

remarks.para: The original has no soldier pass: each HumanSoldier updates where the walk reaches it, its children -- HumanView, Shadow, the gun, then the HumanAI whose CHANNELS packet moves it -- before the next soldier starts. A soldier therefore sees the soldiers before it in the tree where they are this tick, and those after it (and the player, late in ConditionalContainer_560) where they were last tick.

A GuardGenerator (0x487EE0) decides and clones first, then walks its soldier; a Door (0x446D10) and an AlarmControl (0x4408A0) walk their children first, then update. Call before the walk and EndTick after it.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.SoldierWeaponFire.SprayTarget(OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi,OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Where a follow-firing patrol's round goes: along its own facing, at the aim point's height.
member.param: The shooter.
The target's feet, in world units.
Whether the target is crouching.
member.remarks: The follow fire has no burst and no aim solve: the trigger is pressed whenever the target is inside a 16.3° cone about the shooter's forward axis, and the round flies where the BODY points. The port's facing has no pitch, so the ray borrows the aim point's height and keeps the facing's horizontal error — which is the part that decides the spray's geometric misses.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.SoldierWeaponFire.FireIfAsked(OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Player.SoldierView,OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi,OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Turns a raised trigger into a round, at the weapon's own cadence.

remarks.para: The AI never fires: it holds slot 6 down and the weapon decides when a round comes out, which is the split the original has between 0x48D8E0 and the human's weapon tick 0x462E50. The clip is what the AI watches to count its burst, so it has to drain here and nowhere else.
The reload takes the weapon's own Reload Time; both of the AI's two reload routes reach the same place, so they are not told apart here.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.SoldierWeaponFire.SpreadRound(OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi,OpenIGI.Game.Ai.AiStationaryGun,OpenIGI.Game.Weapons.WeaponType,OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.SoldierAgent,OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d,OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d)
member.summary: Where a guard's round really goes: along the gun, with the weapon's cone about it — 0x478BA0, the same Gun_Fire the player's rounds come out of.

remarks.para: Retail's round leaves along the firer's own orientation (the matrix its fire message carries, or the gun's), not along a line to the target, and is then turned by rand³ × the weapon's spread about a random bearing -- the minimum spread for the first four rounds of a pull, the maximum after. A guard only aims by turning its body and view onto the point (to within 2 degrees before it opens fire), so those two errors are all the accuracy it has.

Measured on the retail game with the probe (mission 1, Hard, a stationary guard at 15-22 m): 242 rounds passed 0-3.5 m from the player and 7 hit -- about 3%. Casting every round exactly at the aim point and leaving only the probability roll made 107 of 181 hit.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.SoldierWeaponFire.ThrowAiGrenade(OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Ai.Igi1HumanAi,OpenIGI.Core.Numerics.Vector3d,OpenIGI.Game.Weapons.GrenadeSimulation)
member.summary: Lets a soldier's grenade go at its throw clip's release frame — Soldier_ThrowUpdate (0x45B2F0) into AI_AimThrow (0x452930) and Grenade_Throw (0x477040).
member.param: The thrower.
Where it leaves the hand: the origin plus bone 16's palette offset (motion+0x858).
The pool it flies in.
member.remarks: Two draws from the level's stream, in this order: the flight time in seconds (+15784 plus a share of +15788) and the cook (fistp(rand * +15796 * 30 + +15792) -- the minimum not made ticks). The throw aims at the target's origin raised (0x451380), a tenth past it: delta * 1.1 / (time * 30) a tick, with time * 30 * 22.30044 -- half the fall a tick, times the ticks -- added upward. The cook comes off the grenade's own fuse.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Config.ConfigNatives
member.summary: The fifty-one Config_* functions the menu scripts call.

remarks.para: Registered by the original at 0x402FF0. All but a handful are one-line accessors on the active profile, so they are grouped here rather than spread across fifty-one methods; the ones with real behaviour — the perf-level mapping, profile creation, the list fillers — say where they came from individually.

These are reached through , which hands over the unevaluated arguments. That matters: a volume setter has to pull its argument as a float, and a profile name as a string, and neither would survive the integer walk.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Config.ConfigNatives.#ctor(OpenIGI.Game.Config.GameConfig,OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Config.IConfigHost)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.
member.param: The configuration to read and write.
Supplies what the shell knows: display modes, devices and missions.

member.name: P:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Config.ConfigNatives.Config
member.summary: Gets the configuration these act on.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Config.ConfigNatives.Find(System.String)
member.remarks: The active profile's (0x4061C0).

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Config.ConfigNatives.DefaultOf(System.String)
member.remarks: The original resets the list from its own defaults (0x536410); the port's are a fresh profile's, , as its profiles' own reset gives.

member.name: P:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Config.ConfigNatives.Target
member.summary: Gets the list box a fill call is currently targeting, if any.
member.remarks: The original's fill natives write into whichever control is running its Collect Items Script, which it knows because the expression is being evaluated for that task. Here the manager sets it before running the expression.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Config.ConfigNatives.TryInvoke(System.String,OpenIGI.Scripting.Expressions.ScriptArguments,OpenIGI.Scripting.Runtime.QvmValue@)
member.summary: Handles a call, if it is one of these.
member.param: The function name.
The unevaluated arguments.
Receives the result.
member.returns: when the name is not a Config_* function.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Config.ConfigNatives.ResetGraphics(OpenIGI.Game.Config.PlayerProfile)
member.summary: Restores the graphics settings to what a fresh installation has.
member.remarks: Config_ResetGraphicOptions (0x403B70) is called from Config_ResetToDefaults as well as from the menu's Reset entry, so it is the one place the graphics defaults live.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Config.ConfigNatives.Apply(OpenIGI.Game.Config.PlayerProfile,System.Action{OpenIGI.Game.Config.PlayerProfile})
member.summary: Applies a change, and does nothing when there is no profile to change.
member.remarks: The original dereferences its active-profile pointer unguarded, which cannot be null because a default profile is always created. Refusing rather than faulting is the safer shape and cannot differ on any configuration the loader produces.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Config.ConfigNatives.Fill(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{OpenIGI.Game.Menus.MenuListItem})
member.summary: Puts items into the list box whose collect script is running.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Config.GraphicsPerformance
member.summary: The mapping between a graphics performance level and the flag bitmask it stands for.

remarks.para: The graphics screen has one slider with seven stops and three switches. The slider works in levels and the switches in individual bits, and the two are reconciled through this table — which is why moving the slider flips the switches and flipping a switch moves the slider.
From Config_GraphicOptionsGetPerfFlagsFromLevel (0x4055C0), which indexes the table at 0x537B74 directly and unguarded, and Config_GraphicOptionsGetPerfLevelFromFlags (0x405530), which scans it.

member.name: P:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Config.GraphicsPerformance.LevelFlags
member.summary: The flags each level stands for, highest quality first.
member.remarks: Read out of the binary at 0x537B74, seven entries ending at 0x537B90. The values are not monotonic as integers — they are bit patterns, and level 6 is everything off.

member.name: P:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Config.GraphicsPerformance.LevelCount
member.summary: Gets the number of levels the slider offers.
member.remarks: Config_GraphicOptionsNumPerfLevels.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Config.GraphicsPerformance.FlagsForLevel(System.Int32)
member.summary: Gets the flags a level stands for.
member.param: The level.
member.returns: The flags, or zero for a level outside the table.
member.remarks: The original indexes the table with no bounds check at all, so an out-of-range level reads whatever follows it in the data segment. Returning zero is the one place this deliberately diverges: reproducing an out-of-bounds read would mean reproducing the layout of the executable's data segment, and no shipped script can reach it — the slider is built with exactly stops.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Game.Igi1.Config.GraphicsPerformance.LevelForFlags(System.Int32)
member.summary: Gets the level whose flags are closest to the ones given.
member.param: The flags.
member.returns: The level.
member.remarks: Nearest by Hamming distance, not by equality: the original XORs the argument with each entry, counts the set bits, and keeps the smallest. So flipping one switch away from a level still reports that level, and the slider does not jump. Ties go to the earliest entry, because the comparison is strictly less-than.
